questions.recWhy: The engine is the only thing here that is ours, 3,614 lines with no DOM and measured as portable, so one core behind more than one surface is right and was never in doubt. The order is what changed. The extension route looked like the fast way to a real population, and it still has no estimate, no Live mode, and a niche where the best of thirteen listings has 400 installs. Meanwhile the tools a developer reaches for to do one quick markdown job, dillinger and StackEdit and Excalidraw, show zero sign-in words and an editor on arrival, and our home page is a login screen. Phase 0 fixes that on the web in four weeks, on code that exists. Kiro from AWS is now fighting Cursor for the IDE window, which is one more reason not to open there first. The extension waits, unforeclosed, until someone in the twenty asks for it.

It is also the one feature with a counted vote behind it, 501 likes against 0 for our old headline, on the only forum that votes. Obsidian is different. Freezing is the one answer that needs nothing we do not already have: the shell stays as it is, new work goes to the engine and the one surface, and the merge question waits for the user count.

notes: 14 to 11 cards, a 21% reduction. Facts changed by the briefing: FF1 and FF11 no longer read the VS Code review niche as empty, because Microsoft merged a per-file review/unreview operation into the Agents window on 2026-07-03 (PR 324218, milestone 1.128.0) and documented none of it; the differentiator moves to state stored in the repository, per span, across machines. FF1 and FF14 now carry the four free working-tree agent diffs shipped between 2026-08-24 and 2026-09-03. FF12 gains petergyang/human-review at 1,241 stars in six weeks as the nearest free comparator for the package and plugin route. I did not repeat the refuted VS Code docs claims from briefing §5. Every file:line citation was checked with sed before it was written; the four non-file citations are api.github.com URLs from the briefing's usable table.
